drug_class: CDK4/6 inhibitor (a type of targeted cancer therapy)
purpose: Palbociclib is used to treat a certain type of breast cancer called HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer in adults. It is usually used together with another hormone-blocking medicine. It can be used for breast cancer that has spread to other parts of the body.
how_it_works: Cancer cells grow by dividing and multiplying out of control. Palbociclib works by blocking specific proteins inside cancer cells — called CDK4 and CDK6 — that act like an 'on switch' for cell division. By blocking these proteins, the medicine helps slow down or stop cancer cells from growing and spreading.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is a drop in white blood cells (called neutropenia), which can increase your risk of infections. You may also feel very tired, have nausea, mouth sores, hair thinning, diarrhea, or low appetite. Some people notice headaches or feel weak.
warnings: Because this medicine can lower your white blood cell counts, your doctor will check your blood regularly, especially in the first few months. A low white blood cell count means your body cannot fight infections as well, so tell your doctor right away if you have a fever, chills, or signs of infection. Palbociclib can also harm an unborn baby, so women who could become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for a period after stopping. Men taking this medicine should also use contraception. Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 125 mg taken by mouth once a day for 21 days in a row, followed by 7 days off — making a 28-day cycle. It is taken with food. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have side effects. Always take it at the same time each day and swallow the capsule whole.
